items.title: Sidney "Jim Little" Brown Interview, 1960-05-27
items.q: I went with Sam Morgan for True at that time, see. All the way. I was a Sam Morgan man from that time... Well I played with Sam a while

ctx.x: I think it's the absence of you told me. Yeah. When you came to New Orleans in New York, were you looking for a music job or why did you come to New Orleans?

No I come here to live then. And we got together Sam Morgan and I got together right at that time you see. And we had a little six piece band around then. What were you playing then? I was playing violin. Violin. Uh huh. And it's a little while after I, I wasn't finished growing at the time. And just about the time I was getting big enough to, that I could get tall enough to reach a bass you know? And then I got my Uncle B's violin. Because he had quit playing that time.

items.title: Sidney "Jim Little" Brown Interview, 1960-05-27
items.q: Well who was the drummer then do you remember right back? ... Sam drummer. Sam drummer before the war. Yeah. And uh Yang and all of them played with him then back before the war.

ctx.x: I was wondering about that very first band before the first world war you played with them too you said. Yes. Well who was the drummer then do you remember right back? Well yeah Sam drummer. Sam drummer before the war. Yeah. And uh Yang and all of them played with him then back before the war.

items.title: Sidney "Jim Little" Brown Interview, 1960-05-27
items.q: But he was playing with Faith Morgan on the boat.

ctx.x: How did you take up the tuba then? How did you take up that big instrument?

Well I was with Sam Morgan at the time. Oh you were playing with him again then? Yeah. Yeah. I was playing with Sam Morgan at the time and they quit using the baseball you see. And I just picked that thing up and I said well I'll be if I can learn it. Three or four weeks I had that and gone. And me and Sam Morgan, brother Albert, Albert Morgan. Yeah. I know him. Yeah. We started learning the horn again. But he was playing with Faith Morgan on the boat. See? Yeah. And uh, Sonny Henry took me on that and uh,…

wrap around here or just an upright tuba? No. Upright tuba. Is it B flat or E flat? E flat tuba. E flat. Well that's, that's an E flat tuba. Oh is that E flat? Yeah that's an E flat up there. I thought most of the big things, Pelican and Suzy Phones were B flat. But that's an E flat. Yeah. That's all you ever played in the E flat tuba. I didn't know.
